newsitem.title: USA: PRESS DIGEST - New York Times business - Dec 11.
newsitem.headline: PRESS DIGEST - New York Times business - Dec 11.

text.p: The New York Times reported the following business stories on Wednesday:

- Delta Air Lines unexpectedly said it would place in review its world-wide account, with billings estimated at $100 million, after 51 years with units of BBDO Worldwide in Atlanta and New York and their predecessor shops.
- Volkswagen AG is desperately trying to put an end to the affair over its hiring of the former purchasing star at General Motors.
- Chinese investors have started pouring money into dollar-dominated stocks and China's long-moribund stock markets have suddenly come alive.
- There is a trend in Germany of employing high-wage immigrant workers who come not from poor countries but Europe and other advanced areas.
- Iraq began to pump oil abroad for the first time in six years.
- Investors took profits after Monday's big stock market rally.
- Cotter & Co, owned by True Value hardware dealers, is to form a wholesale company with Servistar.
- Sun Microsystems said more than 100 companies agreed to adhere to rules intended to make Sun's Java programming language the lingua franca of network applications.
- The United States and the European Union appeared close to an accord to pave the way for a global pact to liberalise trade in information technology.
- The Clinton administration said it planned to renew efforts to set rules to prevent the kind of keyboard-related wrist and hand ailments that resulted in a $6 million jury settlement.
- Joseph Stiglitz, chairman of the Council of Economic Advisors, will leave the Clinton administration next year to become chief economist at the World Bank.
- Enron named its No. 2 executive Jeffrey Skilling.
- United Airlines and National Westminster Bank plan to offer a corporate charge card in the United States for use at merchants that accept American Express.
- Malls in Delaware, one of five states with no sales tax, are becoming popular destinations.
